corners.comment: I think I prefer option 3, but the colours from the side should start with the colours they are touching from the gradiant from the top, so it's pink top left and blue top right, try a couple variations on that
corners.reply: Option 3 (the light runs down the sides and fades) is the base. Five new variations, all following your rule: the left side starts in the stripe's pink (the register's --primary) and the right side in its cyan (--accent), exactly the stripe's end colours. They differ in how the light travels: a tube that fades out, on through the ramp toward laser yellow, a short drop of fixed length, a 1 px hairline, and sides that sink into the floor. The old option 3 stays last for reference (its sides start white and are pink on both sides). Square, 2 px controls, nothing notched, nothing flickers.

loading.comment: I want a mix of option 2 and 4. And give me more progressbar options. One of those options should be the progressbar you used to measure the timings in step 1 of this demo. The progressbar from the screenshot should be one of the progressbar options
loading.reply: Ten options. 1 to 4 mix option 2 (the ramp flows through the tube) and option 4 (the floor drives toward you): both at once; the ramp against the drive; the floor fast and the ramp trailing; the floor wearing the ramp's colours. 5 is the three progress bars of step 1 (the curve question: Sync, Backup, Upload with their captions, the lit length charging on the page tube one beat ahead), looping. 6 is the package's own busy bar, unchanged, at full size. 7 to 10 are new progress bars derived from them: the ramp at the package's three weights, slats that count the beats, the bar as the page tube pulled down, and a head that leaves the road behind it. I cannot see your screenshot: if it shows a bar that is not option 5 or 6, name it and I draw that one.

leave.comment: I like 1 and 6, make 3 variations on each of them
leave.reply: Options 1 to 4 are the sun sets through it (the original, then with a laser rim on its lower edge, with its stripes widening as it sets, and with the part sinking with the sun); options 5 to 8 are the sun's slab (the original, then with the horizon line riding its top edge, with a standing beat, and thinning into its stripes). Every leave is 900 ms and every arrival is the leave backwards, measured frame by frame: mirror on every part, no flag.
